title: Driver shot by RCMP dies after surgery
subtitle: Animation artist 'experienced both ends of life'
article: A Vancouver animation artist with a history of emotional problems died in hospital Sunday following surgery after he was shot in a confrontation with the RCMP.
Matthew John Wilcox, 39, was shot Saturday in Deep Cove after allegedly striking several other vehicles during a police car chase.
Witnesses said Wilcox refused to comply with police instructions after colliding with an RCMP cruiser, and he dared police to shoot him.
"The guy... was saying, 'Why don't you kill me? Just kill me now. Why don't you kill me?'" said witness Claire McGivern.
Wilcox's injuries from the shooting were described as non-life-threatening. He was expected to make a full recovery but died in hospital after an apparent heart attack. An autopsy will be conducted.
A friend said Wilcox had been diagnosed 18 months ago with bipolar disorder, swinging from excitation and euphoria to depression.
"He experienced both ends of life - the great challenges and lows. And he managed as best as he could with the lows," David Phillips told CBC News.
Phillips said Wilcox worked on a number of high-profile animation productions.
"If many people remember the cartoons Reboot and Spider-Man - well, Matt was the animator. He did a lot of the animation on those."
An investigation into the role of North Vancouver RCMP in the chase and subsequent shooting is being conducted by the Vancouver Police Department.
